tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: OCL has filed an SLP before the Hon'ble Supreme Court against the common order dated 19.05.2016 of the Hon'ble High Court of Telangana in W.P. (C) No. 6095/2004, which upheld levy of electricity duty @ INR 0.25 per unit on power generated and consumed by consumers. Pursuant to the order, the Chief Electrical Inspector issued demand notices to OCL for INR 16.91 Crores for the period 17.07.2003 to 23.05.2013. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, as an interim measure, directed payment of duty @ INR 0.15 per unit and stayed the balance INR 0.10 per unit, subject to the SLP outcome, and OCL has paid INR 10.05 Crores (duty @ 15 paise per unit) as per Hon'ble Supreme Court's direction. The matter was last listed on 06.11.2024. The matter is to be listed for final arguments in due course.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company has been accused of wrongful availment of Input Tax Credit of Rs 6.46 Crores taken on Construction of Private Railway Siding treating it as "Immovable Property" and not falling under "Plant and Machinary" which are generally used in the course of furtherance of its cement business. Also 100 % Penalty of Rs 6.46 Crores was levied. The Company filed an appeal in March 2025 before Commissioner (Appeals) for which hearing was held on 12.08.2025.

The Company has received an order under Section 92CA(3) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, wherein the DC/ACIT TP 2 Kolkata has recomputed the transfer pricing adjustments related to the transfer of power from the Captive Unit to the Manufacturing Unit. As a result, the DC/ACIT TP 2 Kolkata has ordered that the Assessing Officer increase the Company's income by Rs. 41.22 crore for the AY 2022-23. The Company's original claim was Rs. 11.33 crore, whereas the DC/ACIT TP 2 Kolkata has proposed an addition of Rs. 41.22 crore, which is considered an erroneous adjustment. The final tax demand, including any applicable penalties, will be determined as part of the assessment order. The Company received an Order on June 14, 2025 u/s 154 r.w.s. 143(3) of the Income Tax Act, 1961 wherein the Income tax department has rectified the earlier issued assessment order under section 143(3) read with section 144C(3) the assessment for the AY 2022-23. The Income tax department has rectified Transfer Pricing adjustment of Rs. 412247344 in relation to the transaction of transfer of power from Captive Unit to Manufacturing Unit and accordingly reduce the income of the Company for the AY 2022-23 by Rs. 412247344 and allowance of deduction u/s 80IA of the Act Rs. 113277984 as claimed by the Company. Accordingly, the demand raised in the earlier order dated April 30, 2025 for Rs. 196152736 has been revised to Rs. 491707 as per the order received on 14.06.2025. The Company has a strong case on merit and hence filed an appeal before the Income tax Appellate Authorities within the prescribed timelines.

operating_notes.text: Orient's Q4FY26 cement volumes were 1.6 MnT at 76% capacity utilisation, versus 1.7 MnT in Q3FY26 and nil in Q4FY25 (Orient consolidated only from April 2025).
Ambuja consolidated FY26 volumes were 73.7 MnT (+16%) at EBITDA of Rs 887 per tonne and 16.1% margin.
Imported petcoke CFR rose 35% in Q4 to USD 160/t from USD 119/t, with FY27 demand growth seen at ~5%.
Orient Cement is described as operating at full capacity, versus Sanghi at 65-70% and Penna at 55-60% utilisation guided for FY27.
Ambuja's FY26 cement cost was ₹4,400/t against a ₹4,000/t target, with the March quarter at ₹4,500/t versus a normalized ₹4,250/t.
Ambuja's FY26 volumes were 73.7 MnT (+16%) at EBITDA of ₹887/t and PAT of ₹2,647 Cr, with capacity at 109 MnT.
Combined installed and commissioned cement capacity was 8.50 MTPA as at 31 March 2026 across Devapur, Chittapur and Jalgaon.
Related-party sales to parent Ambuja Cements were ₹1,029.16 Cr and to ACC ₹907.84 Cr in FY26.

The audit trail feature was not enabled for direct data changes for April 1, 2025 to August 31, 2025 (pre-migration software) and September 1, 2025 to February 23, 2026 (post-migration), as disclosed in Note 50.
BSE and NSE observation letters on the Orient Cement–Ambuja Cements scheme are valid six months, within which the scheme must be filed with NCLT.
₹512 Cr of inter-corporate deposits were given to holding company Ambuja Cements at 8% p.a., repayable by March 31, 2027.
Q2FY26 depreciation was higher by ₹63 Cr due to a change in useful life and residual value estimates for PPE and the power plant.
Geopolitical issues had a ₹228 PMT impact on Q2 operating costs.
Trade share increased to 74% in Q2FY27 from 68% in Q2FY26.
Green power share reached 61% at Ambuja consolidated level.

timeline.summary: Q4FY26 results (standalone): revenue ₹647.23 Cr (-21.6% YoY), net profit ₹55.43 Cr (+31.8% YoY).
2026-05-04: Ambuja's Q4/FY26 investor presentation says the Orient-Ambuja merger scheme awaits SEBI's NOC, expected to complete over FY27; Orient's Q4FY26 volumes were 1.6 MnT at 76% utilisation.

2026-05-10: Q4FY26 earnings call transcript filed; Ambuja guides FY27 volume growth at ~8% (industry 5-5.5%), a ₹250/t cost cut in FY27 and another ₹250/t in FY28, and says the 155 MnT capacity target could slip to FY30; Orient Cement described as running at full capacity.
2026-05-29: FY26 integrated annual report filed; standalone PAT ₹337.69 Cr (up 270%) on a ₹19.38 Cr tax credit, unmodified audit opinion, contingent liabilities ₹82.44 Cr.

2026-06-04: BSE and NSE issue observation letters with no adverse objection to Orient Cement's scheme of amalgamation with Ambuja Cements; the scheme still needs shareholder, creditor and NCLT approvals.
Orient Cement reported Q2 FY27 results with EBITDA down 28% YoY to ₹1,271 Cr due to energy costs, while confirming merger completion by January 2027.

upcoming_events.description: Record date for final dividend of Rs. 0.50 per share

Orient quarterly cement volumes and utilisation in Ambuja's next deck
SEBI no-objection certificate for the Orient and Ambuja merger scheme
Requisite approvals for completion of the amalgamation

watchlist.response: Higher branding spend, repairs and maintenance including breakdowns at acquired Penna assets, and premium cement logistics costs.
watchlist.text: Why Ambuja's fixed costs rose faster than peers in Q4FY26

watchlist.response: Management acknowledged the miss, attributed it to acquired assets and packaging costs, and committed to ₹250/t cuts in each of FY27 and FY28.
watchlist.text: Cost guidance credibility after missing the ₹4,000/t target

watchlist.response: Karan Adani said there is partially a reset, moving away from the timeline but not the target, with capex paused to correct execution.
watchlist.text: Reset in capacity ambition from 155 MnT

status_history.evidence: Trade receivables fell to ₹310 Cr at Sep-2026 from ₹840 Cr at Mar-2026, below the ₹839.96 Cr target.
